title: Bayern Munich, Germany forward Serge Gnabry to miss World Cup with thigh injury
content:
Bayern Munich and Germany’s Serge Gnabry has confirmed that will miss the 2026 World Cup after sustaining an adductor tear in his right thigh.

The 30-year-old missed Bayern’s 4-2 win over Stuttgart on Sunday, which confirmed their 13th Bundesliga title in the last 14 years, with the team announcing on Saturday that Gnabry was set to miss an “extended period”.

Gnabry has now been ruled out for the remainder of Bayern’s 2025-26 season, which includes both legs of the Champions League semi-final against Paris Saint-Germain and the DFB-Pokal semi-final against Bayer Leverkusen on Wednesday, as well as the World Cup in North America. He joins Bayern goalkeeper Sven Ulreich and midfielders Lennart Karl and Tom Bischof on the sidelines.

In a post on Instagram, Gnabry said that “the last few days have been tough to process.”

“As for the World Cup dream with Germany…that’s sadly over for me,” he wrote. “Like the rest of the country I’ll be supporting the boys from home.

“Now it’s time to focus on recovery and getting back for pre-season.”

Gnabry had been in good form for Bayern this campaign, scoring 10 goals and providing 11 assists in all competitions.

The forward has been capped 59 times by Germany, scoring 26 goals, and was looking to represent the nation at the World Cup for the second time after starting all three of the team’s group stage games in Qatar in 2022.

Gnabry scored three goals and provided one assist in six appearances to help the national team qualify for this summer’s tournament last year.

Germany begin their 2026 World Cup group stage campaign against Curacao on June 14.
